notes: Round Robin is explicitly categorized under CPU scheduling algorithms.
Time quantum definition is a strict prerequisite for Round Robin execution.
FCFS is introduced as non-preemptive CPU scheduling algorithm.
Convoy effect is explicitly defined in FCFS when I/O processes wait behind CPU-burst job.
Round Robin mitigates convoy effect through time-slice preemption.
SJF is presented as an optimal average-waiting-time scheduling algorithm.
SJF causes indefinite blocking/starvation for lengthy jobs.
Aging technique solves SJF starvation by gradually increasing priority.
MLFQ combines multiple scheduling queues with aging.
Turnaround time defined as completion minus arrival time.
Paging is non-contiguous memory allocation dividing memory into frames.
Page table maps virtual page numbers to physical frame numbers.
TLB is an associative hardware cache inside the MMU.
TLB hit ratio is a primary term in the EMAT formula.
Memory lookup penalty for page table walk is fundamental to EMAT.
Paging eliminates external fragmentation but introduces internal fragmentation in the last frame.
Dynamic storage allocation (first-fit/best-fit) suffers from external fragmentation.
Compaction shuffles memory to combine free holes into one large block.
Compaction is strictly only possible when relocation is dynamic at runtime.
Inverted page tables scale by physical frames rather than virtual address space.
Deadlocks strictly require all four Coffman conditions to hold simultaneously.
First Coffman condition: non-shareable resource holding.
Second Coffman condition: process holding resources while waiting for more.
Third Coffman condition: resources released voluntarily only.
Fourth Coffman condition: closed chain of waiting processes.
Imposing total linear resource order prevents circular wait condition.
Dijkstra's Banker's algorithm tests for safe states prior to allocation.
Classic concurrency synchronization benchmark demonstrating circular wait.
Chopsticks are implemented as mutual exclusion semaphores.
Odd philosophers picking left chopstick first breaks circular wait symmetry.
